glossary.definition: This lab reads route conditions with its own small interpreter. It is not PingGateway, shares no code with it, and cannot show what only a real gateway shows: its real parse errors, route reload and handler chain.

The expression on a route that decides whether a request belongs to it, written as ${ ... }. The lab covers the part real routes use: find(), matches(), contains(), ==, !=, and, or, not, empty and request.uri, request.method, request.headers and request.queryParams.
When two routes match, one must win. The lab assumes routes are tried in name order. Whether real IG does that is UNVERIFIED.

Inside a quoted condition string only \' and \\ are legal escapes. A regex written the natural way, with \., cannot be parsed, so the route is not loaded and its requests get a bare 404. Use [.] for a literal dot. Observed once in a real deployment; here it is simulated.
The header a 401 carries to tell a client how to authenticate: a scheme such as Bearer followed by name="value" params separated by commas.
A comma straight after the scheme, as in Bearer , resource_metadata="...". One real client rejected it. The lab flags it as WA001.
A param in the 401 challenge that points a client at the protected-resource metadata document (RFC 9728), which names the authorization server to use.
The token is valid but too narrow. The answer is 403 with the scope the client should ask for, not 401.
The resource server asks the authorization server whether a token is active and what it carries (scope, aud, exp, client_id). An inactive token gets just {"active": false}.
The lab moves its own clock to expire tokens, so nothing sleeps and a run is repeatable.

sources.title: RFC 6750: The OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token Usage
sources.use: Bearer challenge params, error codes, 401 vs 403 contract

sources.title: RFC 7662: OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection
sources.use: the introspection response the mock AS returns

sources.title: RFC 9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata
sources.use: resource_metadata and the metadata document lint

cards.label: Same path, chosen by host
cards.description: Two routes match the same path. The host condition makes the door route win for its own host, and every other host falls through to the main route.

cards.label: No route matches
cards.description: When no condition is true the gateway answers 404 with no body and no hint. The lab shows each condition and why it was false.

cards.label: A broad route shadows a specific one
cards.description: Both routes match /mcp/{{svc}}. The lab assumes routes are tried in name order, so the broad one answers and the specific one never does. Renaming fixes it.

cards.label: The \. trap
cards.description: Inside a quoted condition string only \' and \\ are legal escapes. Writing the natural regex \. makes the condition unparseable, the route is not loaded, and requests get a bare 404 while everything else looks fine.

cards.label: The [.] fix
cards.description: A character class matches a literal dot with no escape at all, so the condition parses and the route loads.

cards.label: Negative lookahead
cards.description: The main route excludes /mcp/invest and /mcp/weather with (?!...). Those paths fall to their own routes; everything else under /mcp goes to main.

cards.label: Bearer , resource_metadata
cards.description: A script appended ", resource_metadata=..." to a param-less Bearer. The first auth-param is empty. One real client rejected it (reported earlier, not re-measured here).

cards.label: The fixed challenge
cards.description: With a space after the scheme and a comma only between params, the same 401 lints clean.

cards.label: Three ways to break resource_metadata
cards.description: An http URL, an unquoted URL and a missing hint each fail in a different way.

cards.label: Revoked and unknown tokens
cards.description: The mock AS answers {"active": false} and nothing else for a revoked or unknown token. The route turns that into 401 invalid_token.

cards.label: Expiry on the virtual clock
cards.description: Nothing sleeps: the lab moves its own clock. At exp the AS says inactive.

cards.label: Wrong audience
cards.description: The token is active and has the scope, but its aud names a different resource. The route refuses it with 401 invalid_token.

cards.label: Insufficient scope is a 403
cards.description: The token is fine but too narrow. The answer is 403, not 401, with error="insufficient_scope" and the scope the client should ask for.

cards.label: 401 and 403 swapped
cards.description: insufficient_scope on a 401, invalid_token on a 403, and a 403 that forgets the scope each break the contract in a different way.

cards.label: A hostile condition
cards.description: Deep nesting and huge conditions stop at fixed limits with a clear error. Nothing recurses past them and nothing is evaluated.

cards.label: A catastrophic regex
cards.description: The classic (a+)+$ can pin a CPU for minutes. The lab analyses the pattern first and refuses it.

cards.label: The introspection endpoint is down
cards.description: With the mock AS unreachable the route cannot decide. The lab answers 503 and says plainly that how real IG answers here is UNVERIFIED.

cards.label: What is simulated
cards.description: What this lab can and cannot show about real PingGateway.

cards.label: Reading a 401 challenge
cards.description: Scheme, params, resource_metadata and the 401 versus 403 contract.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
